title: Winspace T1600 Review: FAST… But Hard to Control? | NERO Show x JOIN

takeaways.text: Size L (544 mm stack, 392 mm reach) with Dura-Ace, 55 mm wheels, a heavy saddle and pedals weighed 7.6 kg (about 7.4 kg without pedals).
In the show's wind-tunnel test at 50 km/h with the rider aboard it was within test error of a Cervélo S5 and a Quick Pro ER:ONE; bike-only it needed about 109 W against the S5's 100 W.
Build tolerances and brake facing were clean, but the specified 10 Nm seatpost-clamp torque felt worryingly high, and the cylinder saddle clamp let the saddle tilt sideways until carefully balanced.
Rear-end compliance was good and acceleration solid at speed, comparable to the previous-generation S5.

Handling felt twitchy and hard to track at low speed though fine when racing fast; Winspace confirmed via its Australian distributor that the larger-than-usual fork rake is a deliberate choice for a nimble feel. Two other testers agreed it is aggressive-handling.

disclosure: YouTube flags paid promotion for the show's training-app sponsor; the episode does not state how the T1600 was obtained.
summary: Long podcast-style review after about a month: build and spec, a rider-on wind-tunnel comparison with a Cervélo S5 and Quick Pro, and a detailed discussion of the bike's quick, hard-to-settle steering and its fork rake.
